transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Ever since they changed my job around, I’ve sunk into this deep, heavy sadness that I just can’t shake, and it’s getting harder to do anything. I just feel completely exhausted and overwhelmed by everything right now.
How long have you been feeling this way, and have you experienced similar periods of low mood like this in the past?

This heavy, hopeless feeling has been hanging over me for about three months now, starting right around when they announced the company restructuring. I've never experienced a depression this severe in the past, as I'm usually a pretty laid-back person.
Do you feel that your current symptoms are specifically linked to the changes at your job, or would you feel this way regardless of what is happening in your professional life?

I definitely feel like it's directly linked to the job changes. Before they restructured and took away my promotion, I was a pretty laid-back guy and felt stable. But once they put me in that unstable, commission-heavy role, everything just started spiraling out of control.
If the situation at your job were to resolve or change back to how it was before, do you feel that your mood and energy levels would return to your normal baseline?

To be honest, I don't think it would make a difference anymore because it feels like the damage is already done. Even if they gave me my old job back today, this heavy, hopeless feeling is so deep that I don't think my energy would ever go back to normal. I just feel completely stuck in this dark place.
Beyond the stress of your job, have you noticed that you have lost interest or pleasure in almost all of your usual hobbies or activities that you used to enjoy?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in everything I used to love doing. I used to look forward to working on my woodworking projects or going out on the lake with the guys, but now even the thought of doing those things or calling anyone feels pointless and exhausting. I usually just end up staring at the TV without really watching it.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your physical movements, such as feeling like you are moving in slow motion, or have you had recurring thoughts that life is not worth living?

I do feel incredibly heavy and exhausted, but mostly I keep thinking it would be easier if I didn't wake up. I've even pictured driving my truck into a concrete barrier on the highway. I don't want to hurt anyone else, I'm just so tired of feeling like this and screwing everything up.
Have others noticed that you are speaking or moving much more slowly than usual, or do you find yourself so restless that you cannot sit still for even a few minutes?

I haven't really noticed myself moving or speaking slowly, to be honest. While I do get extremely active and talk really fast during my "up" periods, I don't experience that kind of constant physical restlessness or slowness you're asking about.
You mentioned having 'up' periods where you are very active and talk fast; how long do those periods usually last, and have you ever had them when you weren't under this specific job stress?

These "up" periods only started about three months ago when the job stress hit, and I never experienced anything like them before when I had my usual laid-back equilibrium. Now, when I get into those high states, they usually last for several days at a time before I crash back down.
During those 'up' periods where you are very active and talk fast, do you also find that you need much less sleep than usual and still feel completely energized?

Yes, absolutely. On those up nights I’ll only sleep about three hours, if that, but I still pop out of bed feeling completely wired and energized. My brain just runs too hot to waste time lying down, so I feel like I don't even need the sleep.

During those 'up' periods, do you find yourself engaging in risky behaviors—like spending excessive amounts of money, making impulsive decisions, or taking uncharacteristic chances—that you later regret?

I haven't really gone on big spending sprees or done anything physically dangerous. But I do make impulsive moves, like snapping at my boss or calling coworkers late at night with big ideas when I'm in those "up" moods. It's like I just can't stop myself when my brain is running that fast.

During these 'up' periods, does your behavior become so disruptive or intense that it significantly interferes with your ability to work or socialize, or does it primarily manifest as just feeling more energetic and talkative?

Oh, it's way more than just feeling energetic—it has completely disrupted my life. I've snapped at my boss and blown up at customers so much that my manager cut my hours, and I keep calling coworkers at all hours of the night with these erratic business plans. I've also pushed my friends away because I get so easily set off and just blow up at them.

During these 'up' periods where you are acting impulsively and disrupting your work and relationships, do these episodes last for at least one full week, or do they always subside in a shorter amount of time?

I'm not entirely sure of the exact number of days or how long those "up" periods last, because time gets really blurry when my mind is racing. But they definitely seem to go on for quite a while before I finally crash back down.
